narrative.overview:
The archive is Apsara Mode Tailor's shop window seen from a Phnom Penh street. A blue enamel sign board runs full-bleed across the top, its Khmer name painted in yellow above the English. A red-and-white scalloped awning hangs under it, and the section tabs hang from the awning's edge as painted plaques. Below, on a cool tile wall, a row of glass cabinets framed in blue holds one dress each, lit by a yellow lamp strip. The shop's own statement about where its knowledge comes from is a red painted panel, and the page ends on a dark kerb. The look comes from the curator's real source (a family tailor shop, every dress photographed there), never from invented heritage. Nothing sells: no prices, carts or appointments.

The world refuses the museum collection page it replaced: cream ground, a serif headline beside a hero photo, a grid of matted cards. Density is a shop window's: the sign is bold and brief, the counter (heading, count, filters, search) is compact, and the cabinets carry the page. On phones the window becomes a row you swipe along.

The tokens above are normative. In code they are custom properties declared on `body:has(.shop)` in `app/home.css` (`colors.blue` is `--blue`, `colors.shop-ink` is `--shop-ink`, `spacing.frame` is `--frame`), and every rule there is scoped under `.shop`. Archive identity is read from `collection.config.js`, records from `data/garments.js`, and Interface strings from `lib/uiText.js`. Today only the home page (`app/page.js`) wears this system; see **Pages still on The Tailor's Archive** below.
keyCharacteristics: Three paints on a tile wall: enamel blue owns the sign, frames and plaques; yellow is lettering and lamplight; red is the awning, the category label and the source panel.
Big Shoulders condensed sign-writer caps for Latin display. Noto Serif Khmer bold for Khmer display, always above and larger on the sign.
Painted plaques with 2px corners and, when chosen, a fine yellow rule inside the edge. Square cabinets with an 8px blue frame.
Depth is light, not shadow: a glowing lamp strip and a warm spill over each photograph.
Photographs are shown whole on the cabinet's grey back wall, never cropped or recoloured.

rules.name: The Three Paints Rule
rules.body: Blue, yellow and red are the only paints. A fourth accent, a tinted photograph, or a gradient used as a control surface breaks the shop. The awning stripe and the lamp spill are the shop's own fittings, not UI gradients.

rules.name: The Yellow-on-Dark Rule
rules.body: Yellow appears only on blue, red or ink. On white or the wall it fails contrast and is not used.

rules.name: The Words-First Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries meaning alone. A chosen plaque is filled blue with yellow letters and an inner yellow rule, and it also carries `aria-selected` or `aria-pressed`. The chosen language is also bold and underlined. A Status pill always shows its word. An error is always a sentence.

rules.name: The Khmer-Over-English Sign Rule
rules.body: On the sign the Khmer name always sits above the English and is set larger, whichever Interface language is active: 60px against 56px at the top of the range, 4.6vw against 4.2vw between, and the 30px Khmer floor against a 26px English below 640px. Between 640px and 652px both names sit on their 30px floors and are the same size; the Khmer leads from 652px up. This is how a Cambodian shop sign is painted, and it does not swap with the toggle.

rules.name: The Khmer-Is-Content Rule
rules.body: Anything Khmer carries `lang="km"`. Khmer is never uppercased, tracked, truncated, or given a fixed height. Uppercase and tracking on Latin display do not carry into it (every Khmer override resets `letter-spacing` to 0 and `text-transform` to none). Body Khmer uses 1.9 line height, and Khmer in headings 1.5 to 1.6.

rules.name: The Optical-Size Rule
rules.body: Khmer glyphs look larger than Latin glyphs at the same size, so in a mixed heading the Khmer is set smaller than its English partner: 0.72em in a Shopfront `h2`, and 14px Khmer beside the 16px brand. The sign is the deliberate exception (see the Sign Rule): there Khmer leads.

rules.name: The Hanging-Marks Rule
rules.body: Khmer subscript consonants hang below the baseline, so Khmer links put their underline 0.55em below (`a:lang(km)` in `globals.css`). English links put it 5px below.

rules.name: The One-Web-Font Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders, Latin, through `next/font`, is the only font fetched. A second web font, or a web Khmer font, is a system change.

rules.name: The Window Rule
rules.body: Every dress is in its own cabinet in one row of the window: four, three, or a swipe row. Cabinets in a row match in structure; the last cabinet of a short row is not centred or stretched.

rules.name: The No-Sideways-Page Rule
rules.body: The page never scrolls sideways. The only horizontal scrolling is inside the phone filter row and the phone cabinet row, each of which bleeds to the screen edge on purpose and scrolls on its own. Long Khmer wraps by the browser's word breaking, and controls never shrink below 44px.

rules.name: The Lamplight Rule
rules.body: Only the cabinet lamp glows, and it glows yellow. Cards, plaques, panels and the sign cast no shadow. A shadow other than the lamp means "floating above the page", and only the suggestions list floats.

rules.name: The Painted-Edge Rule
rules.body: Nothing a hand presses is rounder than 2px. Categories and filters are plaques, never pills.

rules.name: The Honest-Ornament Rule
rules.body: The awning, frames and lamps are a shop's fittings. No scalloped temple frames, faux Khmer motifs, or generic patterns labelled as authentic.

dos: **Do** read every colour from a custom property whose name matches a token here (`var(--blue)`, never a hex) and scope Shopfront rules under `.shop` until the other pages move.
**Do** put the Khmer name above the English on the sign, larger, in yellow, in every Interface language.
**Do** mark every Khmer string with `lang="km"`, give body Khmer 1.9 line height, and set Khmer in a mixed heading smaller than its English partner.
**Do** mark a choice with words and state as well as paint: blue fill, yellow letters, the inner rule, and `aria-pressed` or `aria-selected`.
**Do** show every photograph whole on the `bay` grey in a 3:4 bay, inside an 8px blue frame.
**Do** keep text contrast at 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and control boundaries), and check the sign, swipe row and counter at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px and at 200% zoom.
**Do** implement in plain CSS or the existing inline objects, with plain JavaScript React components and no new dependencies.
donts: **Don't** put a small label or kicker above a heading. The category label sits under the names.
**Don't** add new Khmer strings without the curator's review. Khmer comes from `lib/uiText.js`, `collection.config.js` and `data/garments.js` as written.
**Don't** set yellow text on white or the wall, add a fourth accent, or tint a photograph.
**Don't** round a plaque, field or panel beyond 2px, or turn filters or categories into pills.
**Don't** add shadows to cabinets, plaques, panels or the sign. Only the lamp glows and only the suggestions list floats.
**Don't** fetch a second web font or a web Khmer font.
**Don't** crop, zoom or recolour a dress photograph, or animate it beyond the one switch-on.
**Don't** substitute a sales funnel, reduce Khmer to decoration, or invent cultural authority.
